newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan tested anti-sub missile in October - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan tested anti-sub missile in October - paper.

text.p: Taiwan successfully test-fired a U.S.-made Harpoon anti-submarine missile in October, bolstering its ability to counter China's modernising navy, a Taipei newspaper reported on Thursday.
The mass-circulation China Times Express, quoting unnamed navy officials, said the missile hit its target in a mid-October test-firing in the sea east of Taiwan.
Taiwan bought 40 Harpoon missiles, each with a range of 80 nautical miles, from the United States, the newspaper quoted the officials as saying.

"This is the first time we have test fired the Harpoon missile and there was no assistance from United States personnel during the firing, increasing the navy's confidence of independent operations," a commander was quoted as saying.
Rival China has poured money into building a blue-water, ocean-going navy and Taiwan presumably needs the Harpoon missiles to counter China's growing submarine fleet.
Taiwan's defence ministry has a policy of not disclosing its weapons purchases and would not comment on the report.
Taiwan has had problems buying advanced weapons from the West due to pressure from China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949.
But Taiwan's economic clout has helped it to buy anti-missile Patriot and anti-aircraft Avenger missiles from the United States and they would enter service in 1999, boosting the island's defences.
The size of the missile purchases has not been disclosed.
Beijing has protested against the sales, maintaining that to arm Taiwan is to interfere in Chinese internal affairs.
Despite switching diplomatic ties to Beijing in 1979 and recognising only the communist Beijing government, Washington reserves a right to provide Taiwan with defensive weapons.

China threatens to recover Taiwan by force if the island goes for independence. Taipei says it opposes independence as a sovereign state and still wants reunification with the mainland, but only after China becomes democratic.
